input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Sections 2.1, 7.1 and 12.3 are all favourable and meet the preferred position (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, declining an Order Form is not a breach or shortfall, no unstated minimum-use charges, no minimum-volume commitment). However, § 2.2 imposes a customer-side exclusive-sourcing obligation making Vendor our sole provider of hosted analytics services for the whole term. That commits 100% of our demand with no reduction or termination right, which functions as a volume restriction on Customer and fails the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, which records that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. Minimal fix: make Vendor a non-exclusive provider and confirm we pay only for Services ordered.

proposal.summary: Remove the customer-side exclusive-sourcing commitment in § 2.2 so fees remain payable only for Services actually ordered.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the requirement that Vendor be our sole and exclusive provider, since our playbook does not accept minimum or take-or-pay style commitments and this clause commits all of our analytics demand for the full term with no reduction right. It also contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services. Customer has no obligation to source exclusively from Vendor or to purchase any minimum volume, and will pay only for Services used or ordered under an Order Form.
